To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. BOB and P-BOB are efficient data structures for dynamic rule tables that are used in IP routers; 2. LMPBOB can be used to represent rule tables with prefixes, and it can be used to implement longest-prefix matching; 3. The number of memory accesses required by LMPBOBs to implement dynamic rule tables is O(logn), where n is the number of rules in the table;

(1) BOB is a dynamic interval-tree structure that permits highest-priority tie breaking and is suitable for dynamic router tables with nonintersecting ranges, (2) PBOB is a dynamic prefix tree structure that is suitable when all rule filters in the router tables are prefixes, and (3) LMPBOB, an enhanced version of PBOB, is suitable when all filters are prefixes and when longest-prefix tie breaking is to be done.

BOB and its variations are the first dynamic router-table data structures that are provably efficient for the most commonly used tie-breakers and that perform each of the dynamic-table operations in a number of cache misses that is linear in logn.

the development of efficient data structures for dynamic router tables.

the development of efficient data structures for dynamic router tables, with the goal of reducing the time required to perform the three basic router-table operations: matching, rule insertion, and rule deletion.
